messages:
sasha: Heads up — saw a perf regression in prod after yesterday's AWQ rollout for mixtral-8b-int8. p50 tokens/sec down ~12% on gen workloads.

lee: @sasha can you paste the trace? which kernel fell back?

sasha: pasted a short trace from a local repro run. Looks like kernel selection flipped to the generic path for the matmuls in the decoder. Snippet: 
```
op: matmul
selected_kernel: generic_mm
fallback_reason: quantized_packed_layout_mismatch
latency_ms: 4.2 -> 5.9
```

maria: that fallback smells like a packing/layout mismatch (RoPE scaling can change how KV is laid out). Which mixtral build + AWQ config did you run?

sasha: AWQ config: `awq_v1_calib.bin` from yesterday's sweep (calibration set = short prompts), model build = mixtral-8b-v2-ropelegacy. Runtime picked `generic_mm` because `awq_packed_mm` check failed on `head_dim` tail detection.

lee: do we have perf counters from the same run (batcher, kv hits, caches)?

sasha: yes — full counters: 
```
batcher: dynbatch
avg_batch_size: 3.1 -> 2.7
seq_len_p50: 512
kv_cache_reads: +18%
L2_miss_rate: +3.7%
mem_bandwidth_util: 72% -> 81%
```

jon: also saw an uptick in headwise reorder ops in profiler. My hunch: AWQ quant produced packed blocks with a different tail alignment; when head_dim doesn't divide packing_width the selector falls back and we lose the optimized path. Mixtral's head_dim is 64 but some quant handlers expect 32/128 packing.

maria: I repro'd locally and forced selector to `awq_packed_mm_v2` for mixtral-8b; p50 recovered to within 1.2% of baseline. Patch idea: prefer `awq_packed_mm_v2` for mixtral variants when `head_dim % 32 == 0` and the quant metadata indicates awq layout. Quick patch: <http://ci/internal/patches/1234|link> :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-canary: mixtral-awq-kernel-fix deployed to canary cluster (3/4 hosts)

lee: canary numbers: regression dropped from 12% -> ~1.5% p50. Nice. Still seeing KV spill noise when seq spikes above 1024 — some requests show short-lived stalls.

sasha: digging into KV traces — when sequence jumps we get a prefetch miss pattern. Hypothesis: calibration prompts were short during AWQ run; the quantized layout + RoPE exponent scaling mismatch causes different memory stride when reading KV, hurting prefetch heuristics. Accuracy delta in eval was small (~0.3% on small calibration) but runtime effect is outsized for long-context gen.

maria: proposed plan: 
1) rerun AWQ calibration with long-context prompts (real customer traces) and compare quant metadata.
2) adjust kernel-selector to check both `awq_packed_mm_v2` and fallback path that handles tail dims gracefully.
3) bump dynbatch target for generation workloads from 3 -> 4.5 to increase utilization.
4) add a KV prefetch warmup when sequence length jumps >512 (warm first token read).

lee: SGTM. I'll open the runtime PR for selector heuristics + dynbatch tuning and add a perf test with seq=2048, randomized head alignment. Will also add a small regression test that asserts no fallback to `generic_mm` for canonical AWQ-metadata cases.

jenkins: build/runtime-unit-tests #2782 passed (linux-x86_64, opt).

sasha: merging once CI is green. After patch lands we should trigger a full canary with longer sequences (customer trace subset).

jon: one more note — Qwen-weights on similar quantization showed a different pattern: they hit `awq_block_mm` reliably because head_dim packing matched block size. So this is model-specific (mixtral vs qwen). We should add a simple model->packing hint table in model catalog to steer selector faster.

maria: agreed. I'll add catalog hint + a short doc in eng-runtime/README about packing expectations.

lee: thanks everyone. Filing follow-ups: runtime PR, AWQ recalibration job, canary plan, model-catalog hint.

sasha: thanks — tagging @ops-bot for monitoring dashboards and adding token-level latency plots to the canary run. :rocket:
